objectives.why: Explicit aim (abstract, p. 2): introduce the DevEx Metrics Compass and report what the 120+ metric dataset reveals; no formal RQs.

method.why: 'Structured curation' (pp. 4-5) without search strategy, inclusion criteria, annotation procedure or reliability; the 20+ leader interviews have no method.

sample.why: 120+ metrics from literature and 50+ organizations (examples named, p. 5); number of papers/sources and how they were selected not reported.

threats.why: Only a three-sentence 'Note' on partial public data and research lag (p. 10); 'Remaining Challenges' (pp. 12-14) covers tool scope, not validity.

evidence.why: Descriptive counts only (45 sources, 72%, 63%); dimension 'times' sum to the 120 metrics and contradict the 'fewer metrics' claim (pp. 9-10).

contribution.why: Open-source metric dataset and navigation tool across DORA/SPACE/Core 4, useful for practice; tool not evaluated, explicitly not a new framework.

P2016.flag: internal inconsistencies: dimension counts labelled 'times' (process 25, enablement 26, quality 20, system 11, output 9, team 6, customer 7, business 16) sum to the 120 metrics, output 9 is below its own examples throughput 27 and produced code 25, and business 16 > system 11/output 9 contradicts 'the further you move ... the fewer established metrics' (pp. 9-10); Fig. 3 caption shows four tracked metrics although the removal is 'not pictured' (five marked on p. 6); DORA given as five metrics with change lead time (p. 2) vs 'original four' with cycle time (p. 9); 'nine' vs 'more than nine' frameworks (pp. 1-2). Own data are the curated metric counts (dataset open-sourced on GitHub, p. 15); the Alex outcome 'a few months after' (pp. 14-15) is a fictional scenario, not data

objectives.why: Explicit aim (p. 2): perceived AI impact across the SPACE dimensions; guiding questions on productivity, dimensions and team adoption (p. 4).

method.why: SPACE-structured survey plus interviews and observation; analysis descriptive only, qualitative coding not described, 'focus groups' (p. 2) never reported.

sample.why: 530 of 3,500 (15%); Microsoft randomized U.S. IC pool with exclusions, externals via networks (pp. 2-3); no demographics; qualitative samples undated.

threats.why: 'Survey Limitations' (p. 3): response bias, perceptions not outcomes, AI-user skew, geographic restriction; non-significance/causality caveat (p. 7); short.

evidence.why: Percentages and means only; Table 2 group n, base rates for 'seven times' and tests missing; multi-agent findings from an unreferenced study.

contribution.why: Useful SPACE lens on AI perceptions with team/organizational moderators and recommendations; perception-only, largely confirms prior findings.

P2020.flag: internal inconsistencies: limitations say the study 'focused on developers who regularly use AI tools' (p. 3) although 25% of respondents report not using AI regularly (p. 3), and the SPACE items are reported for 'AI adopters' without their n; 'focus groups' named in the methodology (p. 2) but never reported; the controlled multi-agent study of eight developers (Sara Chizari, pp. 6-7) is not the authors' data and has no reference entry; 'seven times more likely' and 'four percent less likely' given without base rates or tests (pp. 3-4)

objectives.why: Explicit aim (pp. 1-2): describe EngThrive's principles, metrics, infrastructure and case studies as a scalable productivity-measurement approach.

method.why: Framework description plus internal case studies; 'full methodological treatment ... beyond the scope' (p. 1); control groups and analyses undescribed.

sample.why: Microsoft; tens of thousands in telemetry/survey, case orgs of thousands, ~4,000 and 3,000 developers (pp. 8-11); survey and control-group n missing.

threats.why: No limitations section; passing caveats only (SRE Agent 'not a controlled experiment' p. 11, snow-day confounding p. 10, telemetry maturity p. 3).

evidence.why: Effect sizes without n, tests or intervals; metric 'validation' promised (p. 1) not shown; several figures from a talk [5], a panel [7] or uncited internal research.

contribution.why: New operational framework (speed/ease/quality, thriving guardrail, I2C, BDD) run at Microsoft scale; broadly useful for practice, not independently validated.

P2021.flag: possible exclusion: case-study data not traceable - no n, control-group design or analysis method, methodology declared out of scope (p. 1), some figures sourced to a conference talk [5], a panel [7] or uncited 'internal research' (pp. 6, 9-10) (cf. FT-EC3 precedent P2006/P2010; no contradictions among its own figures found); p. 1 says metrics 'and their validation are described in the sections that follow' but no validation is reported; AI survey shares cited from [6] (arXiv version) differ from the ACM Queue SPACE of AI (P2020): collaboration 49% vs 48%, and the ~10%/~3% culture moderators do not appear there; first author affiliated with DX, a commercial vendor (p. 13)

objectives.why: Explicit aim and two RQs (how managers define and measure developer productivity) stated (p. 2); the ML part has no formal RQ.

method.why: Brief thematic analysis; detailed CRISP-DM pipeline, but labelling undescribed, test split doubles as validation set (p. 3); productivity proxy never validated; app only in Figma.

sample.why: 12 managers from 6 Indonesian software houses well tabulated (Tables 3-4); ML data from one unnamed house, number of developers and labellers not reported.

threats.why: No threats/limitations section; only 'slight overfitting' (p. 15), generic 'limitations imposed by data-driven approaches' (p. 18), ethics as future work.

evidence.why: Tables 5-7 report classifier metrics, but text contradicts them (confusion matrix 828 vs 713 test items; 'fastest training'); productivity claims unevaluated.

contribution.why: Limited: screenshot/URL surveillance classifier with an unvalidated productivity proxy; manager definitions confirm known views; validation is unanimous manager agreement.

P2044.flag: possible exclusion: results contradict own tables (cf. FT-EC3 precedent P2006/P2010) - SVC confusion matrix in the text (378 of 405 and 370 of 423, i.e. 828 instances, p. 15) vs Table 7 support 374/339 = 713 (20% of 3,563) and recalls 0.92/0.84; abstract and p. 14 claim EfficientNetV2B0 'trained the fastest and converged in the fewest epochs', contradicted by Table 5 (1991.0 s, 31 epochs vs InceptionV3 1369.5 s, ResNet50V2 4 epochs); 'macro average of 0.89 on the same metrics' (p. 15) vs Table 7 recall/F1 0.88; labelling procedure undescribed and order of augmented oversampling vs split unclear (leakage risk behind 99.6%); IRB and informed consent 'Not applicable' although developers' screenshots and URLs were recorded (pp. 2, 18)

objectives.why: Explicit aim, five specific objectives, RQ1-RQ2 and hypotheses H1-H2 (pp. 2-3).

method.why: Bayesian causal model fitted to synthetic data whose relations 'were defined according to the proposed causal graph' (p. 5): circular; no real data.

sample.why: No participants or real projects; synthetic dataset size never reported; 'prototypical' CI/CD setting only (pp. 1, 4-5).

threats.why: Sec. 6 'Study limitations' (p. 10) is generic, calls the synthetic data 'observational' and omits the circular data generation.

evidence.why: No coefficients, intervals or tests despite 'statistically significant' claims; Table 2 MAE/RMSE 2.4/3.1 vs Table 5 0.98/1.28; Table 3 variables absent from Table 1.

contribution.why: Illustrative DX-to-release-time causal model; results follow from authors' own simulation assumptions, so practical value is limited.

P2047.flag: below FT-EC3 threshold (<3.0); not empirical; possible exclusion: FT-EC2 (synthetic data only, cf. P2002/P2009/P2124) and FT-EC3 (internal inconsistencies, cf. objectives.why: Explicit aim (multifactorial conceptual model for ASD team productivity) and four RQs, RQ1-RQ4 (pp. 2, 6).

method.why: Fenton & Bieman design protocol, expert content validation (Likert) and exploratory Scrum application; validation perception-only, comparison criteria self-scored (Table 5).

sample.why: Expert funnel 30-17-10 with inclusion criteria (Table 1, p. 7); 110 students at four Colombian HEIs; number of teams and survey instrument not reported.

threats.why: Sec. 5.3 'Threats to Validity' (pp. 17-18): expert count, student generalizability, observer bias, no industrial validation; omits self-scoring bias.

evidence.why: Only aggregate expert means/SD (Table 6) and acceptance percentages; no productivity measured; abstract claims 'real-world scenarios' validation (p. 1).

contribution.why: Structured factor-metric-procedure model with traceability; incremental (extends authors' ICCSA 2025 paper, adds no new factors).

P2048.flag: internal inconsistencies (minor; data traceable, not the P2006/P2010 pattern): collection periods sum to 98.9% (64.4% + 34.5%, p. 15); 23 factors evaluated vs 22 selected without explanation (p. 8); 'exploratory empirical application in real teams' (p. 18) vs student-only validation; experts described as 'professionals' (p. 14) vs MinCiencias-ranked researchers (Table 1, p. 7)

objectives.why: Explicit aim (develop and validate TDIM) and three enumerated gaps it addresses (p. 7); no formal RQs or hypotheses.

method.why: Convergent mixed-methods design stated (Sec. 4), but data access, debt categorization and cost conversions undescribed; announced CFA/SEM not reported.

sample.why: 89 projects, 23 orgs, sectors and inclusion criteria; 412 leaders, 62% of 665 (Sec. 4.2-4.3); orgs unnamed, recruitment not described.

evidence.why: Regression and calibration statistics reported, but abstract's 23%/31% effects not derivable from results (34%/14%, p. 14); undefined TDI; unit mismatches.

objectives.why: Aim stated in one sentence ('presents a holistic model', p. 1) plus motivating questions; no RQs, scope loosely bounded.
